header.units: 1x GUI pixels. One texel of a legacy container sheet = one GUI pixel = one unit here. The integer GUI scale factor multiplies all of this at draw time; see gui_scale.
header.provenance: MEASURED, not recalled. Every rectangle in this file was derived by scanning the pixels of the file named in its 'source' field with System.Drawing, by finding the runs of the slot bevel colours (#373737 top/left, #8B8B8B fill, #FFFFFF bottom/right) along rows and columns. Where a number could not be measured from an image it is marked 'from': 'code' and cited in the fragment. Do not edit a number here without re-measuring the file it claims to come from.
header.owner: ui-04-cells (cell and screen geometry). assets/ui/ui-atlas.json and assets/ui/ui-palette.json are owned by other work and are not touched by this file.
header.checked_by: tools/check-ui-data.ps1 - re-opens the art and proves every cell and panel recorded here is still where it says. Run it after anything regenerates tools/make-hud-sheet.ps1's output or drops a new reference version in.

path_rule: Every record that names a file carries a 'root', naming one of the keys above, and a path relative to it. The repository-relative path is roots[root] + '/' + that path, concatenated as plain strings - no special knowledge and no rewriting. The same map with the same keys and the same strings is in assets/ui/ui-palette.json, and assets/ui/ui-atlas.json spells the same trees as referenceRoot + '/' + path; tools/check-ui-data.ps1 asserts the shared keys still agree. This replaces a header 'reference_root' that ended in '/gui/' while every source began with 'gui/', so every one of the 24 joins produced '.../gui/gui/container/...' and resolved to nothing.
join_key: atlas_id is the id of the same art in assets/ui/ui-atlas.json, and is the only join key between the three files. It is what says that this file's 'generic_9x6' and the atlas's 'screen/generic_54' are one PNG. Where a size appears on both sides, check-ui-data.ps1 compares them.

conventions.anchor_note: origin_x / origin_y are the top-left of the 16x16 ITEM AREA, which is what vanilla's Slot.x / Slot.y hold and what the game draws an item stack at. The painted bevel FRAME is 18x18 and sits one pixel up and left of it. Mixing the two anchors is the single easiest mistake to make here: a whole panel comes out one pixel off and still looks plausible.
conventions.frame_origin: DERIVED, never stored: frame_origin = (origin_x, origin_y) - cell.item_offset_in_frame, and that offset is (1,1) on every cell of every sheet measured. frame_origin_x / frame_origin_y used to be written out beside 19 of the 128 regions and left off the other 109, so a consumer that read the field got the right answer on 15% of rows and a silent 0 - the panel's own corner - on the rest. One table owns it now: cell.item_offset_in_frame.
conventions.origin_space: All coordinates are relative to the panel's top-left corner, NOT to the image file. Most legacy sheets are 256x256 with the panel drawn in the top-left, so 'panel' and 'file_size' are both recorded.
conventions.pitch_zero: pitch_x / pitch_y are 0 for a single slot (cols = rows = 1). Zero is deliberate: origin + i * pitch is still correct for the only valid index, i = 0, and it cannot be mistaken for a measured grid step.
conventions.cell_size: cell_size is the item area, always 16. frame_size is the painted bevel box, always 18.
conventions.well: Some result slots sit in a larger recessed 'well' rather than a plain 18x18 frame. Where present, 'well' is the painted rectangle (panel-relative, outer edge included) and the item area is centred inside its interior.

cell.source_note: The whole 18x18 file. The SHAPE - the 17-long dark L, the 17-long light L, the two #8B8B8B far corners - holds on all 26 legacy container sheets. The COLOURS hold on 25 of them: crafter.png draws its 3x3 grid with #383838 where every other sheet has #373737 (see screens[crafter].regions[grid]), so a detector that matches the dark bevel on an exact colour finds nine cells missing there and nowhere else.
cell.pitch_note: Adjacent cells share their bevel edge, so there are exactly 2 pixels of border between two item areas and the pitch equals the frame size.

edges.corner_note: The two far corners (17,0) and (0,17) are #8B8B8B - neither dark nor white. The dark L and the light L are each 17 long, not 18. Any detector that assumes a closed 18-px box misses every slot.

panel.source_note: Rows and columns scanned at x=120 and y=78. Identical on every sheet measured, and on the Bedrock card at roots.bedrock_icons + '/card-right-full.png'.
panel.padding_note: 3 px of border + 4 px of bare plate puts the first slot FRAME at 7 and the first ITEM at 8. That is where the famous x = 8 comes from; it is not a free choice.

player_inventory_vertical.statement: Let H be the panel height. Player storage first item row y = H - 82. Hotbar item y = H - 24. 'Inventory' label y = H - 94.
player_inventory_vertical.derivation: storage rows occupy 3 * 18 = 54 px from H-82, ending at H-28; the hotbar sits 4 px below that (H-24). Label is 12 px above the first storage row.

chest_height.blit_note: The measured texture is reproduced by blitting the top rows*18+18 pixels of generic_54.png, then its v=126 h=96 strip at y = rows*18+18. A commonly quoted code listing uses rows*18+17 for the first blit, which does NOT reproduce this texture - it lands one pixel short. The texture is the owner.

gui_scale.from: code / documentation, cited in fragment 4.9 - not measurable from an image
gui_scale.algorithm: scale = 1; while (scale != maxScale && scale < fbWidth && scale < fbHeight && fbWidth / (scale + 1) >= 320 && fbHeight / (scale + 1) >= 240) scale++; if (enforceUnicode && scale % 2 != 0) scale++;
gui_scale.auto: GUI Scale 0 means auto, which is maxScale unclamped - the loop runs until the 320x240 test fails.
gui_scale.scaled_size: guiScaledWidth = ceil(framebufferWidth / scale), guiScaledHeight = ceil(framebufferHeight / scale)
gui_scale.consequence: Every number in this file is an integer GUI pixel, multiplied by an integer scale at draw time. Screens are therefore pixel-exact at every scale, and the panel is centred with leftPos = (guiScaledWidth - panelWidth) / 2, topPos = (guiScaledHeight - panelHeight) / 2 in integer arithmetic.
gui_scale.minimum_resolution_note: The 320x240 constants are what the auto-scale loop protects, and a hard 320x240 minimum WINDOW size is a 26.3 change (the SDL3 switch), not a long-standing 1.13 feature.
gui_scale.bedrock_note: Bedrock does not use this loop - its GUI scale is a percentage modifier on a computed base, which is why a Bedrock screenshot can land on non-integer scale factors. Our reference crops in reference/ui-icons are at 1x and 3x.

anchor_trap.where: tools/make-hud-sheet.ps1, comment above the container panel builders
anchor_trap.claim: 'our slot borders sit at x 7, 25, 43 where the reference's sit at 8, 26, 44'
anchor_trap.finding: Both are the same. 7/25/43 are FRAME origins and 8/26/44 are ITEM origins of the very same cells - the reference's frames are also at 7, 25, 43. The comment compares two different anchors, and the 'shift left by one' it justifies is what puts our crafting grid and furnace column 1 px left of the reference. Recorded here, not fixed: this file does not edit source.
